examples.en: Sand got into my shoe, so it's uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 모래알처럼 많은 별이 하늘에 떠 있었어요.
examples.en: Stars as countless as grains of sand filled the sky.
Each grain of sand sparkled in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 손으로 모래알을 한 줌 쥐어 봤어요.
examples.en: I scooped up a handful of sand grains.
I walked barefoot, and the sand grains stung my soles.
A bug as small as a grain of sand landed on my arm.

explain: 모래 한 알 한 알을 가리켜서 아주 작고 많은 것을 비유할 때 써요. '밥이 모래알 같다'는 말처럼 맛이 없을 때도 비유로 써요. 한 알은 '모래 한 알'이라고 하고, 모래 전체는 그냥 '모래'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 감기에 걸려서 밥이 모래알을 씹는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: food tastes like sand
phrases.nuance_ko: 입맛이 없거나 기분이 안 좋아서 음식이 아무 맛도 안 날 때 써요. 실제로 모래가 들어 있다는 뜻은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have no appetite or feel low and food has no taste. It does not mean there is real sand in it.

explain_en: It points to individual grains of sand, so it is used to compare things that are tiny and numerous. It is also used figuratively when food is tasteless, as in '밥이 모래알 같다'. One grain is '모래 한 알', while sand in general is just '모래'.

examples.en: A cheetah runs very fast.
Cheetahs live on the African grassland.
I saw a cheetah for the first time at the zoo.
The rabbit ran away from the cheetah.
Even a cheetah gets tired if it runs for long.
A cheetah's legs are long and slender.

explain: '빠르다'와 함께 자주 나와서 '치타처럼 빠르다'라고 비유로도 말해요. 비슷하게 생긴 '표범'과는 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.en: My younger brother is as fast as a cheetah.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 빠른 것을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A comparison used for being very fast.

phrases.en: That athlete runs like a cheetah.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달리는 모습이 아주 빠를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone runs very fast.

phrases.en: I saw a cheetah running at the zoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진짜 치타가 달리는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a real cheetah running.

explain_en: It often appears with '빠르다', so '치타처럼 빠르다' works as a comparison. The similar-looking '표범' (leopard) is a different animal.

examples.en: The kids are kicking a ball on the grass.
I lay on the grass and looked at the sky.
The grass is wet from the rain and slippery.
I spread a mat out on the grass.
It is faster if you cut across the meadow.
The puppy ran off into the meadow.

explain: 풀이 자란 곳을 가리키고, 사람이 가꾼 곳은 보통 '잔디밭'이라고 해요. '-밭'은 '꽃밭'처럼 무언가가 많이 자라는 땅에도 붙어요.

phrases.en: We sat on the grass and ate our lunch boxes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야외에서 쉬거나 먹을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when resting or eating outdoors.

phrases.en: A puppy is running around on the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀밭 위에서 일어나는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say what happens on the meadow.

phrases.en: I rested on the lawn in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 가꾼 풀밭이에요. 공원이나 학교에 있는 것은 보통 '잔디밭'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A grass area that people take care of, like in parks or schools.

explain_en: It points to a place where grass grows, while a place people take care of is usually called '잔디밭'. The ending '-밭' also attaches to land where something grows a lot, as in '꽃밭'.

examples.en: As evening came, the lake was tinted sky-blue.
My friend came out wearing a sky-blue dress.
That child's eyes are a clear sky-blue.
We went on a picnic on a day when the sky was a lovely color.
Just looking at sky-blue feels refreshing.
I was given a ceramic piece that looks like the color of the sky.

explain: '하늘색'과 거의 같은 색을 말하지만, '하늘빛'은 색 이름보다 하늘에서 느껴지는 빛깔이라는 느낌이 있어서 글이나 시에서 더 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '하늘색'이 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: I bought a sky-blue umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하늘빛'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 이쪽이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 하늘빛, and the more common word in everyday speech.

phrases.en: I hung sky-colored curtains in my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 앞에 붙여 색을 말할 때 써요. '하늘색'보다 부드러운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before an object to describe its color; feels softer than 하늘색.

phrases.en: This color is a clear sky color.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이에요'를 붙여 색을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 이에요 to describe what color something is.

explain_en: It refers to almost the same color as '하늘색', but '하늘빛' feels more like the hue you sense from the sky than a plain color name, so it appears more in writing and poems. In speech, '하늘색' is more common.

examples.en: At the zoo, the hippo opened its mouth wide.
Hippos mostly rest in the water during the day.
The child fell asleep hugging a hippo doll.

examples.ko: 저는 하마를 실제로 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never seen a hippo in real life.
I bought a bag with a mouth as big as a hippo's.
I drew a picture of a hippo and gave it to my younger sibling.

explain: '하마처럼 입이 크다'는 입이 아주 크다는 비유로 쓰여요. 사람에게 쓰면 놀리는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서 조심해요.

phrases.example: 강가에 하마 한 마리가 누워 있어요.
phrases.en: One hippo is lying by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세니까 '하마 한 마리'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with 마리, so you say 하마 한 마리.

phrases.example: 아기 하마가 엄마 옆에서 자고 있어요.
phrases.en: The baby hippo is sleeping next to its mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새끼 하마를 쉽게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say a young hippo.

phrases.en: When it yawns, its mouth is as big as a hippo's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입이 매우 크다는 비유예요. 사람에게 쓰면 놀리는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for a very big mouth. It can sound teasing if used about a person.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a mouth as big as a hippo's

explain_en: '하마처럼 입이 크다' is a comparison meaning the mouth is very big. Said about a person it can sound like teasing, so be careful.

examples.en: We went out to sea on a fishing boat at dawn.
A fishing boat is coming into the harbor.

examples.ko: 낚싯배는 보통 열 명쯤 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: A fishing boat can usually carry about ten people.
I caught a big sea bream on the fishing boat.
The waves were high, so the fishing boat rocked a lot.
I booked a fishing boat for this weekend.

explain: 낚시하는 사람을 태워 주는 배를 말할 때 많이 써요. 고기 잡는 일을 하는 배는 '고깃배'나 '어선'이라고 해요. 배를 세는 말은 '척'이에요.

phrases.en: I take a fishing boat on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탈것을 말할 때 '타다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 타다 to say you ride the boat.

phrases.example: 바다에 낚싯배 한 척이 떠 있어요.
phrases.en: One fishing boat is floating on the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배는 '척'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Boats are counted with 척.

phrases.en: The fishing boat leaves at six in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 떠나는 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to give the departure time of the boat.

explain_en: It is often used for a boat that takes people out to fish. A boat used for the fishing trade is a '고깃배' or '어선'. The counter for boats is '척'.

t90.ax: A fishing boat is coming into the harbor.

examples.en: What is the average starting salary for college graduates?
This company only hires college graduates.
Even college graduates find it hard to get a job.
They surveyed the pay gap between college and high school graduates.
The application requirement is a college degree or higher.

examples.ko: 요즘은 대졸자가 너무 많아져서 경쟁이 심해요.
examples.en: These days there are so many college graduates that competition is fierce.

explain: 구인 공고나 뉴스에서 많이 나오고, '고졸자'와 짝으로 자주 써요. 평소 말할 때는 '대학 나온 사람'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 대학 나온 사람만 지원할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only people who went to college can apply.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대졸자'와 뜻이 같지만 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 대졸자 but a casual way to say it in conversation.

phrases.example: 이번에 대졸 신입을 열 명 뽑아요.
phrases.en: This time we are hiring ten new college graduates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구인 공고에서 처음 일하는 대졸자를 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in job postings for college graduates starting their first job.

phrases.en: The pay is different for high school graduates and college graduates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 학력을 비교할 때 짝으로 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a pair when comparing the two education levels.

explain_en: It appears often in job postings and news, and pairs with '고졸자' (high school graduate). In casual speech people also say '대학 나온 사람'.

t90.ax: This company only hires college graduates.

examples.en: I played rugby with my friends on the weekend.
Rugby has a lot of physical contact, so you have to be careful.
I wonder how rugby differs from soccer.
I like soccer and I like rugby too.
My younger sibling got into university through rugby.
My dad was a rugby player when he was a student.

explain: '축구'는 발로 공을 차는 경기이고, '럭비'는 손으로 공을 들고 달릴 수 있는 경기예요. 공 모양도 달라서 럭비공은 둥글지 않고 길쭉해요.

phrases.en: I watched a rugby game on TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경기'를 붙여 시합을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 경기 to talk about a match.

phrases.en: My uncle was a rugby player in college.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 운동을 하는 사람을 말할 때 '선수'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 선수 to talk about someone who plays the sport.

phrases.en: A rugby ball is long and oval.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공'을 붙이면 경기에 쓰는 공을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 공 means the ball used in the game.

explain_en: In 축구 (soccer) you kick the ball, while in 럭비 you may carry the ball in your hands and run. The ball differs too: a rugby ball is long and oval, not round.

examples.en: I bought clothes whose colors go well together.
The name and the photo don't match.
The shoes go well with the bag, so it looks nice.
Once the information matches, the check is done.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 조건이 매치되었다는 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: I got a message saying their conditions matched.
A message appeared saying the data doesn't match.

explain: 영어 match에서 온 말이라서 옷 색깔이나 정보가 맞을 때 써요. 옷이 어울릴 때는 '어울리다'로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 사람이 주어가 되어 직접 맞출 때는 '매치하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The two colors match well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘'을 붙여서 서로 잘 어울릴 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '잘' to say that two things go well together.

phrases.example: 이 가방은 제 옷과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.en: This bag goes well with my clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 색이 어울릴 때는 '매치되다' 대신 쉬운 '어울리다'를 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: For clothes or colors, the easier '어울리다' can replace '매치되다'.

phrases.en: The name and number match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보가 서로 같을 때는 '맞다'가 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: '맞다' is the easy word for when pieces of information agree.

explain_en: It comes from English 'match' and is used when clothing colors or pieces of information fit together. For clothes that suit each other, you can swap in 어울리다. When a person does the matching, use 매치하다.

t90.ax: The name and the photo don't match.

examples.ko: 여름에는 아이들이 분수에서 물장난을 하며 놀아요.
examples.en: In summer, kids play and splash around in the fountain.

examples.ko: 아이들이 광장 분수 주변에서 물장난을 치며 놀고 있어요.
examples.en: The kids are playing with water around the fountain in the square.
We played with water in the tub, and the whole floor got wet.

examples.ko: 물장난이 너무 재미있어서 아이가 안 나오려고 해요.
examples.en: Water play is so fun that my child doesn't want to get out.

examples.ko: 아이는 수영은 못 해도 물장난만 해도 좋아해요.
examples.en: The child can't swim, but loves just splashing around.

examples.ko: 물장난 때문에 옷이 다 젖어서 갈아입었어요.
examples.en: My clothes got soaked from splashing around, so I changed.

explain: '물장난을 하다'나 '물장난(을) 치다'로 말해요. '물놀이'는 바다나 수영장에서 노는 것까지 넓게 가리키고, '물장난'은 물을 튀기며 장난치는 모습에 가까워요.

phrases.en: We splashed around in the water with our feet by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치다'를 쓰면 물을 튀기며 장난하는 모습이 잘 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '치다', you can picture splashing the water playfully.

phrases.en: The baby plays with the water during a bath.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물장난을 하다'를 한 단어처럼 줄여 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened, one-word form of '물장난을 하다'.

phrases.en: My daughter loves playing with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 가지고 노는 것을 좋아한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say someone likes playing with water.

explain_en: You say '물장난을 하다' or '물장난(을) 치다'. '물놀이' is broader and includes playing at the sea or pool, while '물장난' is closer to playfully splashing water.

examples.ko: 천에 바늘구멍이 나면 물이 샐 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If a needle hole appears in the fabric, water may leak through.
Light came in through a gap as small as a needle hole.
Even a needle hole is small, wind still comes in through it.

examples.ko: 가죽에 바늘구멍을 너무 크게 내지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't make the needle holes too big in the leather.
This year the spots for passing are as narrow as the eye of a needle.

examples.ko: 바늘구멍 크기라도 그냥 두면 점점 커져요.
examples.en: Even a needle-sized hole gets bigger if you leave it.

explain: 실 꿰는 바늘의 구멍은 보통 '바늘귀'라고 하고, '바늘구멍'은 바늘로 뚫은 작은 구멍을 말할 때 많이 써요. 아주 작고 좁다는 느낌 때문에 비유로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Competition is fierce, so passing is like getting through the eye of a needle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기회나 통로가 아주 좁아서 들어가기 매우 어렵다는 뜻이에요. 취업·입시 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the chance or path is so narrow that getting in is extremely hard. Often used about job hunting and admissions.

explain_en: The eye of a sewing needle is usually called '바늘귀', while '바늘구멍' is often used for a tiny hole made by a needle. Because it feels so small and narrow, it is also common in comparisons.

examples.en: My heel got scraped because of the new dress shoes.
I tiptoed quietly with my heels raised.
In winter, my heels get dry and crack.
I put cream on my heels and put on socks.
The heel area hurt, so I went to the hospital.
I wore a long skirt that reaches down to my heels.

explain: 줄여서 '뒤꿈치', 또는 '발꿈치'라고도 해요. 신발의 뒷부분은 '뒤축'이라고 불러요. '발뒤꿈치를 들다'는 발끝으로 서는 느낌으로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: My heels were dry, so I put on cream.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발뒤꿈치'를 줄인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '발뒤꿈치'.

phrases.en: I walked for a long time, so my heels hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발 뒤쪽이 아플 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the back of your foot hurts.

phrases.en: I couldn't reach, so I stood on tiptoe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발끝으로 서는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for standing up on tiptoe.

explain_en: It is shortened to '뒤꿈치' or also said '발꿈치'. The back part of a shoe is called '뒤축'. Note that the phrase '발뒤꿈치를 들다' (raise your heels) is used for standing on your toes.

t90.ax: In winter, my heels get dry and crack.
